facts.fact: Azure resources sit in a hierarchy of Microsoft Entra tenant > root management group ("Tenant root group", ID equal to the Entra tenant ID) > management groups > subscriptions > resource groups > resources (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview).

Azure RBAC role assignments and Azure Policy assignments inherit downward from any scope of the hierarchy, including management groups, subscriptions and resource groups (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview).

Azure Policy assignments inherit downward from management group, subscription and resource group scopes to the resources below (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview).

One Entra directory supports up to 10,000 management groups and a management group tree up to six levels deep (not counting the root or subscription level) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview).

Each management group or subscription has exactly one parent, and all subscriptions in a management group must trust the same Entra tenant (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview).

No one has default access to the root management group; only a Microsoft Entra Global Administrator can "elevate access" to it (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview).

facts.target: Azure RBAC User Access Administrator role
facts.fact: A Microsoft Entra Global Administrator who elevates access gets Azure RBAC `User Access Administrator` at the root management group and can then delegate any Azure role down the hierarchy (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview).

Azure custom roles that contain `DataActions` (which includes most Foundry data-plane custom roles) can't be assigned at management group scope; assign them at subscription or lower (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/governance/management-groups/overview).

Azure is bought through four billing account types: Microsoft Online Services Program, Enterprise Agreement, Microsoft Customer Agreement and Microsoft Partner Agreement for CSP partners (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/view-all-accounts).

A new Microsoft Online Services Program (pay-as-you-go/free/Visual Studio) billing account allows a maximum of 5 subscriptions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/view-all-accounts).

An Azure Enterprise Agreement is structured as enrollment > departments > accounts and allows 5,000 subscriptions per EA account (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/view-all-accounts).

A Microsoft Customer Agreement is structured as billing account > billing profile > invoice section and allows up to 10,000 subscriptions for an enterprise MCA (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/view-all-accounts).
The Microsoft Partner Agreement is the Azure billing account type for CSP partners (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/cost-management-billing/manage/view-all-accounts).

All Azure and Foundry human access is through Microsoft Entra ID user principals (members or B2B guests) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry).

Foundry recommends Entra ID over API keys for production because Entra enables Conditional Access, MFA, managed identities and per-principal RBAC and auditing (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry).

Phase 1: since October 2024 Microsoft enforces MFA for user accounts signing in to the Azure portal, Microsoft Entra admin center and Intune admin center for create, read, update and delete operations (Microsoft 365 admin center from February 2025), with no opt-out (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication).

Phase 2: from 2025-10-01 MFA enforcement gradually applies to user accounts doing create, update or delete through Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, Azure mobile app, IaC tools, SDKs and REST calls to `https://management.azure.com`; tenants could postpone Phase 2 to 2026-07-01 at most (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication).

Managed identities and service principals are not affected by Azure mandatory MFA Phase 2 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication).

For mandatory MFA Phase 2 Microsoft recommends Azure CLI 2.76+ and Azure PowerShell 14.3+ (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication).
For mandatory MFA Phase 2 Microsoft recommends Azure PowerShell 14.3+ (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication).

REST calls to `https://management.azure.com` for create, update or delete fall under mandatory MFA Phase 2 from 2025-10-01 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication).

facts.source: OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password Credentials flow
facts.fact: The OAuth 2.0 ROPC flow (for example `UsernamePasswordCredential`, or `DefaultAzureCredential` with `AZURE_USERNAME`/`AZURE_PASSWORD`) is incompatible with MFA; move automation to workload identities (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication).

facts.source: OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password Credentials flow
facts.fact: The ROPC flow is deprecated in MSAL and Azure Identity libraries as of 2026-11-14 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication).

facts.source: OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password Credentials flow
facts.fact: Resource Owner Password Credentials is an OAuth 2.0 flow (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication).

facts.target: OAuth 2.0 Resource Owner Password Credentials flow
facts.fact: Azure Identity exposes ROPC via `UsernamePasswordCredential` or `DefaultAzureCredential` with `AZURE_USERNAME`/`AZURE_PASSWORD`, which is deprecated and breaks under MFA (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/authentication/concept-mandatory-multifactor-authentication).

Entra service principals are app registrations that authenticate with a client secret, certificate or federated credential (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview).
A system-assigned managed identity has its lifecycle tied to one resource and costs nothing extra (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview).

A user-assigned managed identity is a standalone resource attachable to many resources and is Microsoft's recommended type for Microsoft services; managed identities cost nothing extra (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry).

Entra ID tokens for Foundry use scope `https://ai.azure.com/.default` against endpoints like `https://<resource>.services.ai.azure.com` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry).

Foundry token auth requires a custom subdomain on the Foundry resource, and a 401 usually means the wrong scope (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry).

Foundry API keys grant full access to the resource with no role restrictions, no per-user attribution and no Conditional Access; Microsoft advises removing key auth (disable local auth) after callers move to tokens (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).
Foundry Agent Service, evaluations and Toolbox don't support API keys at all (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry).

facts.fact: A new Azure AI Search service defaults to key-based authentication; you must switch the service to "Both" or "Role-based access control" or all RBAC-token requests are denied (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac).
If a request to Azure AI Search carries both a key and a token, the key wins (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac).
Azure AI Search data-plane token scope is `https://search.azure.com/.default` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac).

A user-assigned managed identity or an app registration can trust tokens from an external OIDC issuer (GitHub Actions, any Kubernetes cluster including EKS/GKE, Google Cloud, AWS via IAM Outbound Identity Federation, SPIFFE/SPIRE, Azure Pipelines service connections) and exchange them for Entra access tokens with no stored secret (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation).
Workload identity federation trusts tokens from external OIDC issuers (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation).

GitHub Actions can exchange its OIDC tokens for Entra access tokens through workload identity federation with no stored secret (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation).
Any Kubernetes cluster, including EKS and GKE, can federate to Entra through workload identity federation (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation).
AWS workloads can federate to Entra via IAM Outbound Identity Federation (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation).
Azure Pipelines service connections can use workload identity federation to get Entra tokens (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation).
A federated identity credential's `issuer`, `subject` and `audience` must match the external token case-sensitively (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation).

Entra-issued tokens can't be used as the external token in a federated credential flow, and Entra caches only the first 100 signing keys from the external issuer's OIDC endpoint (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identity-federation).

An app registration can hold at most 20 federated identity credentials when using managed identities as FIC (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/managed-identities-azure-resources/overview).
Entra access tokens get a random default lifetime of 60-90 minutes (75 average) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/access-tokens).
Tenants with Continuous Access Evaluation get long-lived Entra tokens of 20-28 hours, revocable by CAE events (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity-platform/access-tokens).
Role assignments granted to a managed identity can take several hours to take effect because managed identity tokens are cached (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac).
Managed identities and workload identity federation are free (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identities-faqs).
Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium is listed at $3 per workload identity per month on the page dated 2025-03-18 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identities-faqs).

Workload ID Premium adds Conditional Access and ID Protection for workload identities (single-tenant service principals only; managed identities aren't eligible), access reviews and app health recommendations (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identities-faqs).

Conditional Access for workload identities requires Microsoft Entra Workload ID Premium and applies to single-tenant service principals only, not managed identities (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/workload-id/workload-identities-faqs).
Microsoft Entra Agent ID, an identity type made for AI agents, is generally available (what's-new page dated 2026-05-01) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/whats-new-agent-id).

Entra Agent ID adds agent identity blueprints, agent identities, agent identity blueprint principals and agents' user accounts, plus agent-specific OAuth flows, Conditional Access, ID Protection and ID Governance (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/whats-new-agent-id).

An agent identity blueprint templates agent identities and holds their credentials; OAuth permissions granted to a blueprint apply to all its agent identities, it can apply Conditional Access to all of them, and disabling it stops all of them authenticating (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/agent-blueprint).

A blueprint's only tenant operation is provisioning or deprovisioning agent identities via the Graph permission `AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/agent-blueprint).

An Entra agent identity is a special service principal created from a blueprint; it is always single-tenant even if the blueprint is multitenant, and the blueprint is authorized to impersonate it (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/agent-blueprint).

In the current Foundry agent model, creating an agent provisions a unique blueprint and a default-instance agent identity that starts with no resource permissions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).

Legacy Foundry agents share a project-level blueprint and identity, and migrating changes the identity so downstream role assignments don't transfer (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).

Foundry puts a federated identity credential on each blueprint that trusts the first-party "Azure Machine Learning" app (`0736f41a-0425-4b46-bdb5-1563eff02385`) acting in your tenant (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).

Foundry blueprints are keyless: no secret or certificate exists, and neither project, agent code nor project managed identity holds the credential (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).
Code in a Foundry hosted agent gets tokens for its own agent identity through the hosted-agent token service (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).

The project managed identity isn't available to hosted-agent code, and each hosted-agent session runs in a VM-isolated sandbox with no blueprint credential (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).

facts.fact: A Foundry agent identity acting on behalf of the signed-in user (for example Work IQ, Foundry MCP, Azure DevOps MCP, Fabric IQ, Dataverse) is in preview as of 2026-11-14 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).
On-behalf-of agent access needs the preview `AgentBlueprint` endpoint authorization scheme (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).

Foundry on-behalf-of agent access (preview) covers targets such as Work IQ, Foundry MCP, Azure DevOps MCP, Fabric IQ and Dataverse (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).

Entra Agent ID documents integration (sidecar and federation patterns) for agents on AWS, GCP and n8n, including a guide to secure an Amazon Bedrock agent (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/whats-new-agent-id).
Entra Agent ID documents sidecar and federation integration patterns for n8n agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/whats-new-agent-id).
Entra Agent ID offers migration guides from custom app registrations and from Copilot Studio agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/whats-new-agent-id).
Microsoft recommends the Microsoft Agent 365 CLI and SDK for agent identity provisioning and runtime token acquisition (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/faq).
The Microsoft Agent 365 CLI is recommended for provisioning Entra agent identities (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/faq).
Microsoft recommends `Microsoft.Identity.Web.AgentIdentities` for .NET agents using Entra agent identities (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/faq).
Microsoft recommends the Microsoft Entra ID Auth SDK (sidecar container) for non-.NET or containerized agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/faq).

Agent identities can't sign in through Entra sign-in pages, so they can't use OIDC or SAML single sign-on; the admin consent workflow also doesn't work for agent identity permission requests (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/faq).

Non-Microsoft platforms using app-only permissions can create at most 250 agent identities per blueprint (Foundry and Copilot Studio are exempt); soft-deleted agent identities are restorable for 30 days (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/faq).
Sequential Graph creates of agent objects can fail with `400 Object ... not found`, so add retries with backoff (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/faq).

Conditional Access for agents requires Microsoft 365 E7 (includes Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Suite) (page dated 2026-07-31) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/agent-id).

Alternatively, Conditional Access for agents requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license paired with at least Microsoft Entra P1 or Microsoft 365 E3 (page dated 2026-07-31) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/agent-id).
Microsoft 365 E7 includes Agent 365 and Microsoft Entra Suite (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/agent-id).

For on-behalf-of access the policy must target the user; for app-only access target the agent identity or its blueprint; for agent-user access target "Agent Users" (policies scoped to "Users" don't apply to agents' user accounts); policies don't apply when an agent uses an API key (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/conditional-access/agent-id).
Foundry agent identities appear in the same tenant-wide Entra admin center inventory as Copilot Studio agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).
Agent registry experiences are converging under Microsoft Agent 365 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/whats-new-agent-id).

Microsoft Agent 365 became generally available worldwide on 2026-05-01 (secondary) (https://www.licensingschool.co.uk/licensing-blog/2026/03/23/agent-365-ga-announcement/ ; https://www.itelio.com/en/microsoft-message-center/MC1296867).

Microsoft Agent 365 is reported at $15 per user per month standalone and included in Microsoft 365 E7 (secondary, as of 2026-11-14) (https://www.licensingschool.co.uk/licensing-blog/2026/03/23/agent-365-ga-announcement/ ; https://www.itelio.com/en/microsoft-message-center/MC1296867).

Azure Logic Apps Standard enables a system-assigned managed identity by default (Consumption must enable it manually); both plans can carry one system-assigned plus multiple user-assigned identities (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/logic-apps/authenticate-with-managed-identity).
Logic Apps Standard hybrid deployment doesn't support managed identity and needs an app registration (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/logic-apps/authenticate-with-managed-identity).

Azure API Management authenticates to Foundry/Azure OpenAI backends with its managed identity via the `authentication-managed-identity` policy with `resource="https://cognitiveservices.azure.com"` (or a backend with managed identity credentials) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-authenticate-authorize-ai-apis).

Azure API Management validates inbound Entra tokens with the `validate-azure-ad-token` policy (or `validate-jwt` for other IdPs) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/api-management-authenticate-authorize-ai-apis).

Microsoft Entra directory roles (for example `Global Administrator`, `Application Administrator`, `Agent ID Administrator`) govern the directory and Graph (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/authorization-agent-id).

Azure RBAC roles (for example `Owner`, `Foundry User`) govern Azure resources at management group, subscription, resource group, resource, project or agent scope, separately from Entra directory roles; agents may need both plus Graph permission grants (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/authorization-agent-id).

Azure RBAC role `Azure AI User` was renamed `Foundry User`; role ID and permissions are unchanged, old names may still appear, and Microsoft advises using role GUIDs in code (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).

Azure RBAC role `Azure AI Account Owner` was renamed `Foundry Account Owner` with unchanged role ID and permissions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).
Azure RBAC role `Azure AI Project Manager` was renamed `Foundry Project Manager` with unchanged role ID and permissions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).

facts.fact: Foundry role GUIDs: `Foundry User` = `53ca6127-db72-4b80-b1b0-d745d6d5456d`; `Foundry Owner` = `c883944f-8b7b-4483-af10-35834be79c4a`; `Foundry Account Owner` = `e47c6f54-e4a2-4754-9501-8e0985b135e1`; `Foundry Project Manager` = `eadc314b-1a2d-4efa-be10-5d325db5065e`; `Foundry Agent Consumer` = `eed3b665-ab3a-47b6-8f48-c9382fb1dad6` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/ai-machine-learning).

Azure RBAC `Foundry User` grants reader access to the Foundry resource and project plus all `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/*` data actions; it's the least-privilege role for developers building and testing agents and for the project managed identity on the Foundry resource (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/ai-machine-learning).

The actions of `Foundry User` also include `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/listkeys/action` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/ai-machine-learning).

Azure RBAC `Foundry Agent Consumer` has a single data action `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/AIServices/endpoints/interact/action` and is the least-privilege role for users or service principals that only call agents (for example the Responses API) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/ai-machine-learning).

The Azure portal assigns `Foundry Agent Consumer` only at Foundry account scope, so use `az role assignment create` for project or agent scope (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).
`az role assignment create` assigns `Foundry Agent Consumer` at Foundry project or agent scope, which the portal can't do (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).

Azure RBAC `Foundry Project Runtime User` (`142bfaed-a13f-4c2d-bed2-6db62c4a1009`) is a minimal runtime role whose data actions are `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/AIServices/responses/read`, `/write` and `/delete` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/ai-machine-learning).

Azure RBAC `Foundry Project Manager` can create projects, build in them, publish agents and assign only the `Foundry User` role (ABAC-constrained) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).

`Foundry Project Manager` is the minimum role on the Foundry resource to publish agents, and the recommended role for agent creators who must grant `Foundry User` to a new agent identity (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

Azure RBAC `Foundry Account Owner` can create Foundry accounts and projects, deploy models and conditionally assign `Foundry User`, ACR and monitoring roles (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).
`Foundry Account Owner` has no data-plane rights, so it can't build or call agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).

Azure RBAC `Foundry Owner` combines control plane and data plane (create accounts/projects, manage models, build, publish, call agents); Microsoft calls it a highly privileged self-serve role (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).
`Foundry Owner` is the only built-in role that can both fine-tune and deploy a fine-tuned model (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).

Azure RBAC `Owner` and `Contributor` can create Foundry accounts, projects and deployments but can't create agents or call agent endpoints, because they carry no Foundry data actions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).
Azure RBAC `Contributor` carries no Foundry data actions, so it can't create agents or call agent endpoints (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

Azure RBAC `Azure AI Developer` (`64702f94-c441-49e6-a78b-ef80e0188fee`) and `Azure AI Administrator` apply only to Azure Machine Learning workspaces and Foundry hubs, not to Foundry projects or hosted agents; don't use them for Foundry projects (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/ai-machine-learning).
`Azure AI Administrator` applies only to Azure Machine Learning workspaces and Foundry hubs (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).
`Azure AI Developer` grants access on Azure Machine Learning workspaces and Foundry hubs only (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).

Microsoft says not to assign `Cognitive Services *` roles for Foundry work except `Cognitive Services Usages Reader` (`bba48692-92b0-4667-a9ad-c31c7b334ac2`, subscription scope, for quota and deployment-eligibility views) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

`Cognitive Services OpenAI User` (`5e0bd9bd-7b93-4f28-af87-19fc36ad61bd`) still applies when code calls the account-level OpenAI endpoint directly (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).
`Cognitive Services User` (`a97b65f3-24c7-4388-baec-2e87135dc908`) applies for calling Speech, Vision or Language directly (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).

Azure RBAC `Cognitive Services OpenAI Contributor` (`a001fd3d-188f-4b5d-821b-7da978bf7442`) adds deployment write/delete and RAI policy (guardrail) management to all `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/OpenAI/*` data actions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/role-based-access-control/built-in-roles/ai-machine-learning).

facts.fact: Minimum Foundry setup: assign `Foundry User` on the Foundry resource to the developer and to the project managed identity (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).

The Foundry portal assigns `Foundry User` to the developer and project managed identity automatically when the project creator can assign roles, but not when the resource or project is created by SDK or CLI (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/rbac-foundry).

Foundry doesn't assign RBAC roles to a new agent identity; grant it access on each downstream resource (Azure RBAC, service data-plane roles such as Cosmos DB, or Graph app permissions) using the agent identity's object ID, preferring resource or resource-group scope (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).

A Foundry agent has implicit access to model inference through its project endpoint and session storage without a role assignment (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

A narrow custom role with `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/AIServices/responses/*`, `.../agents/*/read` and `.../agents/*/write` is the documented least-privilege option when explicit agent project access is required (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

For hosted agents, grant the project managed identity `Container Registry Repository Reader` (or `AcrPull`) on ACR and `Log Analytics Data Reader` on the Log Analytics workspace (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

The project managed identity of a hosted agent needs `Log Analytics Data Reader` on the Log Analytics workspace (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).
The hosted-agent deployer needs `Container Registry Repository Writer` (or `AcrPush`) on ACR (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).
Hosted-agent trace viewers need `Monitoring Reader` on Application Insights (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).
ACR used for Foundry hosted agents must have `azureADAuthenticationAsArmPolicy` enabled (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

facts.target: Azure RBAC User Access Administrator role
facts.fact: Only Azure RBAC `Owner`, `User Access Administrator` or `Role Based Access Control Administrator` on the target resource can create the ACR and Log Analytics role assignments for hosted agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

`Foundry Project Manager` and `Foundry Account Owner` are constrained to assigning `Foundry User`, so they can't create the ACR and Log Analytics role assignments for hosted agents (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

Sending the `x-ms-user-identity` header to a hosted agent requires data action `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/AIServices/agents/endpoints/UserIdentityImpersonation/action` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

The UserIdentityImpersonation data action is in no built-in role (it was removed from `Foundry User` and `Foundry Owner`), so create a custom role for the middle-tier identity (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

In Foundry Agent Service standard setup the project managed identity needs `Cosmos DB Operator` and `Storage Account Contributor` at account level (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/standard-agent-setup).

In standard setup the project managed identity needs `Search Index Data Contributor` and `Search Service Contributor` on Azure AI Search (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/standard-agent-setup).

In standard setup the project managed identity needs `Storage Blob Data Contributor` on `<workspaceId>-azureml-blobstore` and `Storage Blob Data Owner` on `<workspaceId>-azureml-agent` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/standard-agent-setup).

In standard setup the project managed identity needs `Cosmos DB Built-in Data Contributor` on database `enterprise_memory` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/standard-agent-setup).

Standard setup is a Foundry Agent Service setup mode whose project managed identity needs Cosmos DB, Storage and AI Search roles (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/standard-agent-setup).

Azure AI Search data-plane role `Search Index Data Reader` (`1407120a-92aa-4202-b7e9-c0e197c71c8f`) allows query and knowledge-base retrieve (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac).
Azure AI Search data-plane role `Search Index Data Contributor` (`8ebe5a00-799e-43f5-93ac-243d3dce84a7`) allows load and query (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac).

`Search Service Contributor` (`7ca78c08-252a-4471-8644-bb5ff32d4ba0`) manages indexes, indexers and knowledge bases but can also retrieve admin keys (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac).
Azure AI Search data roles can be scoped to a single index via CLI, PowerShell or REST only (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac).

Creating Azure RBAC role assignments requires `Owner`, `User Access Administrator`, `Role Based Access Control Administrator`, or a custom role with `Microsoft.Authorization/roleAssignments/write` at the target scope; on the client side this is usually the subscription owner or cloud platform team (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/concepts/authentication-authorization-foundry).

`Role Based Access Control Administrator`, like `Owner` and `User Access Administrator`, can create Azure RBAC role assignments at its scope (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-security-rbac).

facts.source: Microsoft Entra Privileged Role Administrator role
facts.fact: Entra `Privileged Role Administrator` manages directory role assignments (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/identity/role-based-access-control/permissions-reference).

Entra blocks agent identities from highly privileged directory roles such as `Global Administrator`, `Privileged Role Administrator` and `User Administrator`, from role-assignable groups and from administrative units; an allow-list of lower roles (for example `Directory Readers`, `Global Reader`, `Fabric Administrator`, `Power Platform Administrator`) can be assigned (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/authorization-agent-id ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/faq).
The Entra `Global Administrator` role can't be assigned to agent identities (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/authorization-agent-id).

No admin can grant agent identities `Application.ReadWrite.All`, `RoleManagement.ReadWrite.All`, `User.ReadWrite.All` or `Directory.AccessAsUser.All`; lower-privilege delegated (for example `Mail.Read`) or app permissions (for example `User.Read.All`) remain allowed with consent (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/authorization-agent-id).

Lower-privilege delegated Graph permissions such as `Mail.Read` and app permissions such as `User.Read.All` can still be granted to agent identities with consent (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/authorization-agent-id).

Agent identity blueprints support inheritable permissions: an admin grants a permission once on the blueprint principal and every agent identity from that blueprint inherits it (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/agent-blueprint).
"Required resource access" on a blueprint is only a declaration and grants nothing (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/agent-blueprint).

Microsoft Fabric workspace roles are Admin, Member, Contributor and Viewer; only Admin can create a workspace identity or connect Git (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/fundamentals/roles-workspaces).
Entra service principals can be assigned Fabric workspace roles with the same API permissions as users (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/fundamentals/roles-workspaces).

A Fabric administrator controls "Service principals can call Fabric public APIs" (enabled by default for new customers) and "Service principals can create workspaces, connections, and deployment pipelines" (disabled by default), both scoped to allowed security groups (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/fabric/admin/service-admin-portal-developer).

A Foundry resource's public network access flag can be Disabled (private endpoint only, target sub-resource labelled "account"), "Enabled from selected IP addresses", or All networks; DNS uses a `privatelink` subdomain zone, and only Approved private endpoints carry traffic (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).

Foundry inbound network isolation uses private endpoints with target sub-resource "account" and a `privatelink` DNS subdomain zone (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).

Foundry Agent Service outbound isolation injects the agent client into a customer subnet delegated to `Microsoft.App/environments` (size /27 or larger) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).

Agent Service outbound settings can't be changed after creation (redeploy to add injection), and private endpoints for Storage, AI Search and Cosmos DB aren't auto-created (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).
VNet tool calls from Foundry Agent Service need a project-level capability host (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).

In network-isolated Foundry, MCP (private), OpenAPI, Azure Functions and A2A tools go through your subnet; Azure AI Search and File Search through private endpoints; Code Interpreter and function calling over the Microsoft backbone; Bing, web search and SharePoint grounding over public endpoints (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).
A2A tools are supported in network-isolated Foundry and route through the customer subnet (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).
OpenAPI tools are supported in network-isolated Foundry and route through the customer subnet (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).

In network-isolated Foundry the Logic Apps tool, Browser Automation, Computer Use, Image Generation and Fabric Data Agent are not supported (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).

Foundry projects created after 2026-06-25 support a private Azure Container Registry (public access disabled) for hosted agents; older projects need the registry reachable on its public endpoint (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/hosted-agent-permissions).

facts.fact: An AI Gateway (API Management) created from the Foundry portal for a private Foundry resource is automatically public; network isolation for the gateway must be configured in the Azure portal (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).
AI gateway in Foundry is in preview as of 2026-11-14 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities).
The AI gateway in Foundry is an Azure API Management instance created from the Foundry portal (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).

A network-restricted Foundry resource can allow trusted services `Microsoft.CognitiveServices`, `Microsoft.Search` and `Microsoft.MachineLearningServices` through when their managed identity holds the right role (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/how-to/configure-private-link).

For Foundry Models sold by Azure, including Azure OpenAI, prompts, completions, embeddings and training data are not available to other customers or to OpenAI or other model providers, aren't used to improve providers' models, and aren't used to train foundation models without permission (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/openai/data-privacy).
Azure OpenAI models are stateless and don't call OpenAI-operated services; customer data isn't shared with OpenAI (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/openai/data-privacy).
Azure OpenAI is among the Foundry Models sold by Azure (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/openai/data-privacy).

Standard and Regional Provisioned deployments process prompts within the resource's Azure geography; DataZone types process within the Microsoft-defined data zone (US, EU via the EU Data Boundary which may include EFTA countries such as Norway and Switzerland, or APAC); Global types may process in any region; data at rest stays in the customer geography for all types (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/openai/data-privacy).

The EU data zone for DataZone deployment types uses the EU Data Boundary, which may include EFTA countries such as Norway and Switzerland (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types).

Global deployment types such as `GlobalStandard` may process prompts in any region, while data at rest stays in the customer geography (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types).

Deployment type SKU names are `GlobalStandard`, `GlobalProvisionedManaged`, `GlobalBatch`, `DataZoneStandard`, `DataZoneProvisionedManaged`, `DataZoneBatch`, `Standard`, `ProvisionedManaged` and `DeveloperTier`; new models arrive Global first, then Data Zone, then geography-based (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types).

`DeveloperTier` is for fine-tuned model evaluation only, with a 24-hour lifetime and no SLA or data-residency guarantee (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types).

An Azure Policy rule on `Microsoft.CognitiveServices/accounts/deployments/sku.name` (for example denying `GlobalStandard`) enforces data-residency choices across subscriptions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types).

Data stored by Responses API, Assistants threads, stored completions, Files and vector stores stays in the Foundry resource in the customer's geography, is AES-256 encrypted with optional customer-managed keys, and can be deleted anytime; preview features may not meet all these conditions (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/openai/data-privacy).

Foundry Agent Service standard setup stores files in your Azure Storage, vector stores in your Azure AI Search and conversations and agent metadata in your Cosmos DB for NoSQL (at least 3000 RU/s) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/standard-agent-setup).

Standard setup needs a customer Cosmos DB for NoSQL with at least 3000 RU/s for conversations and agent metadata (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/standard-agent-setup).
Standard setup stores agent files in the customer's Azure Storage (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/standard-agent-setup).
Standard setup stores vector stores in the customer's Azure AI Search (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/standard-agent-setup).

Foundry Agent Service basic setup uses Microsoft-managed resources instead of customer-owned Storage, AI Search and Cosmos DB (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/standard-agent-setup).

Models sold by Azure run abuse monitoring: flagged prompts and completions are reviewed by automated means (LLMs) first and by authorized Microsoft employees only when needed, through Secure Access Workstations with JIT approval; for EEA deployments the reviewers are in the EEA (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/abuse-monitoring ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/openai/data-privacy).
The abuse-monitoring store sits in the resource's geography (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/openai/data-privacy).

Customers managed by a Microsoft account team or in an eligible program can apply for modified abuse monitoring via a Limited Access form; once approved, the resource shows capability `ContentLogging` = `false` in its JSON view or `az cognitiveservices account show`, though automated review may still run (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/openai/concepts/limited-access ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/openai/data-privacy).

Foundry guardrails (previously content filters) are named collections of controls covering Hate, Sexual, Self-harm, Violence, user prompt attacks, indirect attacks, protected material (text and code), PII (preview), Task Adherence (preview), Groundedness (preview, models only) and Spotlighting (preview, models only) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview).
Foundry models default to the `Microsoft.DefaultV2` guardrail (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview).

facts.fact: Guardrails for Foundry agents are in preview as of 2026-11-14 and add tool call and tool response intervention points (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview).

An agent's assigned guardrail fully overrides its model's guardrail, and an agent with none inherits the model deployment's guardrail (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview).
Guardrails apply only to Foundry Agent Service agents, not other agents registered in the Foundry Control Plane (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview).

Foundry hosted agents support network egress controls (preview as of 2026-11-14) configured in the same guardrail (RAI policy) to limit outbound destinations (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview).

Network egress controls for hosted agents limit outbound destinations and are configured in the guardrail (RAI policy) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview).

All customers can set blocking levels and turn off content harms for inputs, but turning guardrails off for outputs requires approval through the "Limited Access Review: Modified Guardrails" form, available only to Microsoft-managed customers or eligible programs (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/openai/limited-access).
Groundedness detection (preview) in Azure OpenAI retires on 2027-04-30; other guardrail controls are unaffected (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/guardrails/guardrails-overview).

For Claude in Foundry, "Hosted on Azure" keeps prompts and outputs on Azure infrastructure, while "Hosted on Anthropic infrastructure" may process data outside Azure and outside the selected geography (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/claude-models/data-privacy).

For Claude in Foundry, Anthropic is the seller and an independent data processor under Anthropic's DPA and Commercial Terms in both hosting options (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/responsible-ai/claude-models/data-privacy).
Foundry provides no built-in content filtering for Claude at deployment time (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/claude-models).

Hosted-on-Azure versions of several Claude models (for example `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-haiku-5-5`) are available as Data Zone Standard in the US only; Data Zone Standard isn't offered for Claude in Europe or APAC (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/claude-models ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-from-partners).
`claude-opus-5-5` has a hosted-on-Azure version available as Data Zone Standard in the US only (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/claude-models).
`claude-sonnet-5-5` has a hosted-on-Azure version available as Data Zone Standard in the US only (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/claude-models).
`claude-haiku-5-5` has a hosted-on-Azure version available as Data Zone Standard in the US only (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/claude-models).

Entra sign-in logs can be filtered by agent type (blueprint, agent identity, agent's user account) and show delegated user context (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).
Entra audit logs record blueprint and identity creation/deletion with `agentType` and `blueprintId` (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).
Foundry tracing to Application Insights shows tool calls per agent (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/agents/concepts/agent-identity).

Entra audit logs don't distinguish agent identities by default: operations on agent objects land in the ApplicationManagement category, agent-initiated operations appear as service principals, and Graph activity logs show agents as applications (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/entra/agent-id/faq).

Azure API Management's AI gateway (all tiers) offers `llm-token-limit` (TPM or quota per key), `llm-emit-token-metric`, semantic caching (`llm-semantic-cache-store`/`-lookup`), `llm-content-safety`, and prompt/completion logging to Azure Monitor (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities).
The AI gateway capabilities are available in all Azure API Management tiers (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities).
Azure API Management offers exposure or passthrough governance of MCP servers and A2A agent APIs (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities).
Azure API Management can govern A2A agent APIs through exposure or passthrough (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/api-management/genai-gateway-capabilities).

In Azure public cloud, Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Search, API Management, Logic Apps, Functions, Microsoft Fabric, Private Link and Copilot Studio are in FedRAMP High and DoD IL2 scope (list last updated February 2026) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-government/compliance/azure-services-in-fedramp-auditscope).

In Azure Government, Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search reach DoD IL6, and the Microsoft Foundry portal and Azure AI Content Safety are FedRAMP High and IL2 (list last updated February 2026) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-government/compliance/azure-services-in-fedramp-auditscope).
Azure OpenAI is available in Azure Government at DoD IL6 (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-government/compliance/azure-services-in-fedramp-auditscope).

Azure publishes ISO 27001, SOC 1/2/3, HIPAA BAA, PCI DSS and EU Data Boundary offerings through Microsoft's compliance offerings pages; per-service scope for Foundry was not confirmed in this pass (unverified) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/compliance/).

Azure OpenAI and other models sold by Azure bill per 1M tokens (input, cached input, output) on Standard types, per Provisioned Throughput Unit on provisioned types, and Batch at 50% off Global Standard with a 24-hour target; prices weren't rendered on the page on 2026-11-14 (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/cognitive-services/openai-service/ ; https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types).

Provisioned Throughput Units bill hourly, or with monthly/yearly reservations, with a minimum of 15, 25 or 50 PTUs depending on the model (https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/cognitive-services/openai-service/).
Batch deployments bill at 50% off Global Standard with a 24-hour target (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/foundry/foundry-models/concepts/deployment-types).
